title: Land the Nightly Crash Hotfix on Release 2.1
description:
**SITUATION:**

Production still runs `release/2.1`. Overnight the nightly board-summary job crashed on empty sprint boards and paged on-call — and tonight's run will crash again unless the right fix lands on that release line.

Someone already hot-patched `release/2.1` with a **temporary** batch helper in `src/sprints.py` that just returns the card count — no empty-board guard. That is not safe for production. Priya fixed it properly this morning: clamp the batch size so an empty board cannot blow up. She committed it on `main` as a `HOTFIX`: … but two **unreleased** capacity-planning commits sit under that tip. Those must **not** ship in 2.1.

Ops needs **only** her production-safe clamp on `release/2.1` before tonight's deploy — not the capacity work under it on `main`, and not the release line's naive temporary helper. Bringing all of `main` onto the release would break the freeze. Get her fix onto the release tip. If Git stops because both sides touched the same helper, keep **Priya's safe empty-board clamp**, clear the conflict, finish applying the fix, then update `origin` so Ops can see it. Do not change or push `main`.

You are Ada Learner. Open `~/sprint-service` — you start on `main`. `origin` is `git.forgeboard.internal`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Find the hotfix commit on `main` (subject starts with `HOTFIX`:).
2. Get **only** that fix onto `release/2.1` — the release tip should gain one new commit and must not pick up unreleased capacity work.
3. If Git stops on `src/sprints.py`, resolve using the situation (keep Priya's safe clamp; remove conflict markers), then finish applying the fix.
4. Update `origin` with the new `release/2.1` tip so Ops can deploy. Do not push `main`.
5. Leave the working tree clean; leave `main` untouched. Optionally write the hotfix SHA (from `main`) to `~/answers/hotfix-sha`.

hints: git log --oneline main — find the commit whose subject starts with HOTFIX: (the empty-board batch clamp). Capacity commits sit under it; you want only the hotfix.
git switch release/2.1 then git cherry-pick <sha>. Merging main would bring src/capacity.py into the release — that fails the lab.

The pick will stop on src/sprints.py: release already has a temporary helper, the HOTFIX rewrites the same function. Keep Priya's safe empty-board clamp (if card_count <= 0 → return 1; else min with the batch cap). Remove every <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> marker, git add src/sprints.py, then git cherry-pick --continue.
After the pick, origin still has the old release tip. Publish with: git push origin release/2.1. Plain push is enough — the tip only moved forward.
Leave main exactly as you found it — do not push or rewrite it. Optional: echo the hotfix SHA into ~/answers/hotfix-sha.

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Cherry-Pick the Nightly Crash Hotfix

Production runs `release/2.1`. That line already has a temporary `digest_batch_size` with no empty-board guard. Priya's real fix is on `main` (`HOTFIX:` …) but two unreleased capacity commits sit under it — merge would drag those into 2.1. Cherry-pick **only** the hotfix onto the release tip; Git will stop on `src/sprints.py`. Keep her safe clamp, continue, then push `release/2.1` so Ops can pick it up. Leave `main` alone.

## 1. Find the hotfix

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
git log --oneline main
```

Copy the SHA whose subject starts with `HOTFIX:`.

## 2. Cherry-pick onto the release branch

```bash
git switch release/2.1
git cherry-pick <hotfix-sha>
```

Git stops on `src/sprints.py` — release's temporary helper vs Priya's clamp.

## 3. Resolve the conflict

Keep **Priya's** production-safe empty-board clamp (`if card_count <= 0: return 1`, then `min(card_count, …)`). Drop the temporary `return card_count` helper. Delete every conflict marker.

```bash
nano src/sprints.py
grep -nE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)' src/sprints.py   # should print nothing
git add src/sprints.py
git cherry-pick --continue
ls src/   # no capacity.py
```

Exactly one new commit on the release tip beyond the pre-pick tip. New SHA is expected — that is normal for a cherry-pick.

## 4. Push the release tip

A local cherry-pick does not update the forge. Ops needs `release/2.1` on `origin` before tonight's deploy. Plain push — the tip only moved forward:

```bash
git push origin release/2.1
```

Do **not** push or rewrite `main`.

## 5. Optional

```bash
mkdir -p ~/answers
echo <hotfix-sha> > ~/answers/hotfix-sha
```

## Notes

- Merging `main` into `release/2.1` fails the lab — unreleased capacity lands with it.
- Keeping the release's temporary helper fails — the empty board still crashes.
- Leave `main` exactly as you found it.
- This lab has no pull-request UI; the push is the finish line.
